The core operator is a Manhattan distance over normalized performance vectors. Each of the 17 WhoScored features is scaled using min-max normalization, then summed across dimensions to compute a scalar likeness score. This approach assumes equal weight for all features and linear additivity. The method fails when features are highly correlated (e.g., passes and key passes), leading to redundancy. It also lacks predictive validity since it does not correlate similarity with future outcomes such as fantasy points or transfer value. The lack of train/test splits or cross-validation implies no statistical rigor in assessing generalizability. The use of raw season totals without per-90 normalization introduces bias due to playing time variation. Robust scaling would mitigate outlier sensitivity, while role-based filtering could improve relevance. The method is descriptive rather than predictive, limiting its utility in forecasting or strategic planning.
